author: L. R. Drake
title: Scalise honors law enforcement during Police Week and discusses Republican support
text:
Steve Scalise, U.S. House of Representatives from Louisiana's 1st district | Official U.S. House Headshot
Steve Scalise, U.S. House of Representatives from Louisiana's 1st district | Official U.S. House Headshot
House Majority Leader Steve Scalise said on May 13 that House Republicans are committed to supporting law enforcement officers and their families. Scalise made these remarks during Police Week, alongside Speaker Mike Johnson, House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain, and Congressman Mike Ezell.
Police Week is a time to honor the men and women who risk their lives daily to keep communities safe. Scalise said it is especially important to remember those who have died in the line of duty. “Every week, we pay tribute to our men and women in uniform, our law enforcement officers who keep our community safe. But this week is a special week where we all come together as Police Week to pay tribute to especially those law enforcement officers who paid the ultimate price. Over 100 last year that were killed in the line of duty protecting our communities.”
He recalled a recent tribute at the Capitol steps led by Speaker Johnson with family members of fallen officers present. “Sheriff [Mike] Ezell said it so eloquently – last night, we had a wonderful tribute on the Capitol steps that the Speaker led... And it was tear-jerking to hear those stories,” Scalise said.
Scalise also spoke about his personal experience with law enforcement's bravery: “I would not be alive today if not for the bravery of law enforcement officers... He got through armed, and his intention was to come in and kill the President of the United States and, frankly, kill everybody else he could that was in that room. But he never got there because law enforcement went to the danger.”
He outlined legislative efforts by House Republicans during Law Enforcement Week: “We're bringing a number of bills to the floor this week in remembrance of Law Enforcement Week... We're also bringing a really important resolution by Zach Nunn... They want to defund them at every level, and we will not let it happen.”
Steve Scalise has represented Louisiana’s 1st district since 2008 after replacing Bobby Jindal; he previously served in both chambers of Louisiana’s state legislature according to the U.S. House of Representatives. Born in New Orleans in 1965, Scalise currently lives in Jefferson and holds a Bachelor of Science degree from Louisiana State University according to the U.S. House of Representatives.
